clue.text: In a war, they oddly fight, bringing up unrelated issues

indicators.note: In says one piece is placed inside the other, the bout going in among the shuffled letters
oddly suggests the letters of a war, they behave strangely and are rearranged

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match or fight

explanation.surface: An observer notes how combatants in a war behave strangely, deflecting with irrelevant complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like a call for alternate letters, but here it shuffles A WAR THEY into WHATAERY; 'In' puts BOUT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Whataboutery is the tactic of deflecting criticism by raising some other, unconnected grievance.

clue.text: Properly spoiled with lots of cash

parts.note: to do something properly is to do it well
food that has spoiled has gone off

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly pampered because they are rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well-off means being wealthy, having plenty of money to spare.

clue.text: Removing crap in the pipes is what a trainee plumber might do?

definitions.text: what a trainee plumber might do

indicators.note: read as re-moving, moving the letters of crap in the pipes about again

explanation.surface: Clearing blockages from drains is the grim lot of a junior plumber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removing' is read as 'moving again', so CRAP IN THE PIPES is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee plumber serves an apprenticeship, the period of training under a qualified tradesman.

clue.text: In the end, extra efforts only take it so far

indicators.note: In the end points to the final letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that extra effort only gets you so far.
explanation.definitionFit: As yet means up to now, the same as so far, in time rather than distance.

clue.text: One guy — mad — frequently found in public smoking area

indicators.note: found in says these letters sit inside the word for public

parts.note: something public is open to all
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: frequently means at regular intervals, so every other letter of guy mad is taken

explanation.surface: A wild-eyed man keeps turning up in the outdoor smoking zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frequently' takes alternate letters of GUY MAD, giving UMD.
explanation.definitionFit: An opium den is a place where people gather to smoke the drug, a smoking area of a disreputable kind.

clue.text: Connection on a phone from somewhere in Asia

indicators.note: on a phone means we only hear the word, as said aloud down the line

parts.note: a tie is a link or connection

explanation.surface: A caller is linked by phone to someone in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Thai describes someone or something from Thailand, a country in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Special dog, large rather than small

indicators.note: rather than means the first letter named takes the place of the second

parts.note: a red setter is a breed of dog, the Irish setter
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A dog-show remark: this one is unusual, a big one instead of a small one.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a special or memorable one, from saints' days printed in red on calendars.

clue.text: Party also featuring, on occasion, the right electronic music equipment

parts.note: in legal language a party to a contract is a person

indicators.note: featuring means the word also has the following letters included within it
on occasion means only now and then, so every other letter of the is taken

parts.note: E is short for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A party with, now and then, the proper electronic sound kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' is a legal term for a person; 'featuring' places the inner letters within ALSO, after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal stereo is a portable cassette or CD player with headphones, like the Walkman.

clue.text: Lost piece of Hockney art safely mounted

indicators.note: mounted says the hidden letters are read backwards
piece of says the answer is a fragment taken from inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A David Hockney artwork, securely hung, has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read 'Lost piece' as the definition, leaving no hidden-word signal; 'piece of' is that signal, and 'mounted' in a down clue means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray has been mislaid or wandered off, so it is missing.

clue.text: Fresh cosmetic product

definitions.meaning: fresh in the sense of cheeky or impertinent

explanation.surface: A newly launched item of make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lippy is both an adjective for mouthy or insolent and a casual noun for lipstick.

clue.text: Tech gadget — mini perhaps — containing a tracking device

parts.note: the iPad is Apple's tablet, a tech gadget
a mini is a type of short dress, so an example of a dress

explanation.surface: An iPad Mini sounds like a gadget with a tracker built in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mini' wants to be the iPad Mini; it is the short skirt-length dress.
explanation.definitionFit: An IP address identifies a computer on a network, letting its activity and location be traced.

clue.text: In due course, it can fatten your salary

definitions.meaning: extra hours worked for extra pay

explanation.surface: A promise that eventually your pay packet will grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Over time means gradually; overtime is extra paid work beyond normal hours, swelling wages.

clue.text: Cut out sound made by security device

indicators.note: sound made by says we want the word said aloud, not written

parts.note: a sensor detects intruders, a security device

explanation.surface: Remove the noise an alarm system makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To censor material is to cut out or suppress the parts judged unacceptable.

clue.text: Before the sign to stop, absolutely nothing is produced

indicators.note: Before puts the word for absolutely nothing ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: FA is short for sweet FA, British slang for nothing at all
a red light is the signal to stop

explanation.surface: Nothing whatever came of it before the stop signal appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: To have fathered something is to have originated or produced it, as a father begets a child.

clue.text: To put it mildly, he is upset with me taking up space at the back

indicators.note: upset means the letters of he is, me and up are knocked over into a new order
at the back takes the final letter of the word space

explanation.surface: A tactful report that he is upset with me hogging space at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' shuffles HE IS + ME + UP into EUPHEMIS; 'at the back' adds E, the last letter of 'space'.
explanation.definitionFit: To euphemise is to express something in milder, gentler words, softening an unpleasant truth.

clue.text: Rotten telecoms company stealing money

indicators.note: stealing means the company takes the money into itself

parts.note: Sky is a British broadcasting and telecoms company
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A rotten phone company is robbing its customers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stinky smells foul, as rotten food does; also used for nasty or unpleasant.

clue.text: High-speed train routes are mostly screwed up

indicators.note: screwed up means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means most of the word are is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A passenger complains that most of the fast train's routes are botched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims ARE to AR; 'screwed up' shuffles ROUTES + AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurostar is the high-speed rail service linking London with Paris and Brussels via the Channel Tunnel.

clue.text: Stomach a cold tart primarily containing mushroom

indicators.note: containing means the mushroom sits inside the other letters

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of tart

parts.note: a cep is an edible mushroom, the porcini

explanation.surface: Can you face a cold mushroom tart?
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate or accept it, however unpalatable.

clue.text: Charity hosts round tables, at first virtually

indicators.note: hosts means the charity word takes the round letter inside it

parts.note: alms are gifts to the poor, charity
O is round in shape

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of tables

explanation.surface: A charity holding a round-table event, at first only online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' tempts as online; it is the definition, meaning nearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtually means nearly or all but, so it can replace almost.

clue.text: Utter brute — one who fights

indicators.note: Utter as a verb means speak, so we want the word as pronounced

parts.note: a gorilla is a large ape, or a thug

explanation.surface: A description of a thoroughly brutish fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning complete; it is the verb, to say aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerilla is a member of an irregular armed band fighting a stronger force.

clue.text: One doesn't place leads from such old routers in a computer linkup!

indicators.note: in says the first letters go inside the network

parts.note: LAN is a local area network, linking computers

indicators.note: leads from means the opening letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: An exclamation about old routers in a network that never perform.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a horse or competitor that finishes outside the placings, a loser.

clue.text: Messi's shot goes wide?

indicators.note: shot means damaged or ruined, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lionel Messi's shot fails to hit the target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a football kick; it means wrecked, and shuffles MESSI'S.
explanation.definitionFit: When a shot goes wide it misses the goal, so the striker misses.

clue.text: Young guy lacking restraint in empty clubs and bars

parts.note: a boy is a young male

indicators.note: in places the unrestrained letters inside the emptied word
empty means clubs loses all its middle letters

parts.note: OTT is over the top, excessive, lacking restraint

explanation.surface: A young lad runs wild in deserted nightclubs and pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like drinking places; it is the verb, to shut out.
explanation.definitionFit: To boycott is to refuse to deal with, so it shuts out or bars someone.

clue.text: A number of students in college getting left behind

parts.note: ass is American slang for the backside, one's behind

explanation.surface: Some students at college are being left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a group of pupils taught together, a set number of students.

clue.text: Backchat coming from crass assistant

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Cheeky retorts from a tactless helper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sass is impudent talk, cheek, the same as answering back.

clue.text: Self-styled Adonis is unusually tense

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of Adonis is appear in an odd order

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A vain hunk is strangely on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Soi-disant is French for so-called, claiming a title one has given oneself.

clue.text: Clothes horse is more upright with the front part lifted

indicators.note: lifted in the sense of stolen, so the opening letter is taken away

parts.note: fairer means more honest, more upright

explanation.surface: A drying rack stands straighter when its front is raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' suggests raising; it means stolen, removing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a frame for drying laundry on, which is what a clothes horse is.

clue.text: Worried about no work being sent back for course assistant?

indicators.note: about means the word for worried is turned round

parts.note: stressed means anxious or worried

indicators.note: being sent back means these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An anxious worker is returned for having nothing to do on a training course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests training; it is a course of a meal, pudding. STRESSED reversed gives DESSERTS; NO OP reversed gives POON.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert spoon is the cutlery that helps you eat the pudding course.
